title: FREE 4 days Upper Lower sheiko inspired Bodybuilding Program
summary: NH presents a free 4-day upper/lower program rebuilt from Griffin's Sheiko exercises, for late novices to intermediates: bench supersetted with rows, OHP with chin-ups, squats, good mornings, snatch-grip rack pulls, deadlifts, pin squats, block pulls, plus supersetted small muscles. Template 2 adds week-to-week variation. All sets go to failure within rep ranges, with no percentages.
claims: Not for novices; late novices to intermediates can run it as is, advanced lifters must adapt it
Upper/lower is one of the most convenient templates and a base for body part splits
End the week with the lower day (Saturday) to get maximum recovery from the most gruelling session; upper days need less
Days are Monday, Wednesday, Friday, Saturday but can move as long as the lower day precedes the longest rest
If you need variety you can program it intelligently, e.g. a two-week rotating template, without hurting gains
Superset bench with rows to fit horizontal pulls; dumbbell rows standing on both feet are best when you do not want long warm-ups or lower back strain
No percentages: push every set to failure and get max reps; when the top of the range gets easy, add weight
For lifts or rep ranges you never practiced, start easy without failure to adapt, then push to failure
You do not need to cycle intensity super low or high for bodybuilding
Bodyweight chin-ups for AMRAP; weighted ones for 6-10 reps
Supersets are essential to accumulate tonnage in small muscles that need little recovery; do not skip them
Horizontal presses need a lot of volume for intermediates to progress, hence bench twice a week plus close grip
Supersetting small muscle groups does not impede performance
Heavy deadlifts 3x4-6, or just one set if three is too much
Pin squats start at the reversal point, exactly your parallel, and you must be tight before driving up
The last lower day should leave you beat up but without lower back pain, since you get lots of recovery after it
Template 1 builds balanced strength and size
Week 2 of template 2 swaps in incline bench, deficit deadlifts, dips and dumbbell bench, and fewer squat sets to protect the lower back
Snatch-grip deadlifts plus pause squats already kill the hamstrings, so hyperextensions are dropped that week
Putting calves and neck after block pulls in a superset also gives more rest between block pull sets
I make programs for free and will not sell them; I would rather you learn to program yourself
exercises: standing on both feet, no knee on bench
horizontal pull with good stretch and little lower back strain
start at parallel, tight before driving
